title: You Think Pain Travels Straight Up One Wire, Yet Fast Touch Slams Your Spine Shut
description:
Clinical Case Briefing — Ronald Melzack & Patrick Wall (1965): Spinal Gate Control Theory of Pain, grounded in Ronald Melzack, Patrick D. Wall (1965) (Science). Empirical findings show that published in Science on November 19, 1965, by MIT colleagues Ronald Melzack and Patrick Wall, Gate Control Theory overthrown 300 years of René Descartes's 'bell-rope' pain model.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how thalamus, somatosensory cortex, brainstem coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that before 1965, medicine assumed pain traveled up a dedicated, unmodifiable wire from skin injury straight to a pain bell in the brain — leaving doctors dismissing chronic or phantom pain patients as 'hysterical'.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Ronald Melzack, Patrick D. Wall (1965). Pain Mechanisms: A New Theory. Science. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.150.3699.971
- Juan Carlos Acevedo González (2011). Abriendo la compuerta para el entendimiento del Dolor (Ronald Melzack, Patrick D. Wall-1965). NeuroTarget. https://doi.org/10.47924/neurotarget2011281
- Juan Carlos Acevedo González (2012). Teoría de la compuerta (Ronald Melzack y Patrick D. Wall, 1965). Universitas Médica. https://doi.org/10.11144/javeriana.umed53-4.tcrm
